text: Real Estate Entrepreneur
Born and raised in Seal Beach, I am Scott Davis, 48, a real estate entrepreneur running for District 1.

My education included McGaugh, McAuliffe, and Los Alamitos High; I also participated in Seal Beach Junior Lifeguards. My parents met and married here. In the 1980s, they owned John’s Food King Market on Main Street, where I learned service and the value of local business. My dad volunteered as a firefighter at Seal Beach Fire Station 44, instilling respect for service.

After graduating from the University of Arizona, I built a 20-year media and entertainment career with Paramount Pictures, 20th Century Fox, and Amazon, across the United States and overseas. Returning home in 2023 renewed my appreciation. I serve on the board of Save Our Beach’s Seal Beach chapter, helped launch a kids’ surf camp, and am a Seal Beach Boardriders Club member.

I am running to give back with practical leadership: protect public safety; maintain our beach, pier, streets, and drainage; keep Main Street local; and preserve Seal Beach’s character. I support transparent spending, balanced budgets, strong reserves, and responsible cost reductions before asking more of residents. I will listen, engage, and pursue smart improvements for today and future generations.

text: CEO/Nonprofit Boardmember

As your neighbor, I understand why so many of us choose to call District 1 home, from Old Town to Surfside. Our small-town character, beautiful coastline, welcoming neighborhoods, and locally owned businesses make our community special and deserve protection for future generations.

I have spent years building trusted partnerships with local, state, and federal agencies, law enforcement, schools, businesses, nonprofits, and residents. I believe trust is earned by listening, bringing people together, and following through.

I am running for Seal Beach City Council because local government should be accessible, accountable, and responsive to the people it serves. District 1 deserves a council member who is available, answers the phone, shows up at community events, and welcomes conversations about the issues residents care about most.

My priorities are protecting public safety, preserving our neighborhoods and coastline, securing long-term beach sand replenishment, revitalizing Main Street and preserving the small-town character that makes District 1 so special.
I’ve been endorsed by Seal Beach Mayor Lisa Landau, Orange County Supervisor Janet Nguyen, Orange County Sheriff Don Barnes, and Assemblymember Diane Dixon.
I respectfully ask for your vote.

Phone: (714) 471-8388
Email: perla@perlaforsealbeach.com
Website: perlaforsealbeach.com

text: Sports Broadcaster

I’d be honored to represent District 1 as your City Council Representative. We’ve lived in the area since 2004 and in Old Town since 2019. This is the heartbeat of our special city and I intend to keep Seal Beach as strong as ever with many mounting challenges ahead.

I graduated from Pepperdine University with the intent of attending law school but dream jobs got in the way. From working on-air and as music director at KROQ, to my 30-year career in sports broadcasting, I’ve been blessed to wake up and do what I love every day.

I’ve spent considerable time the past few decades around championship DNA: Kobe Bryant, Clayton Kershaw, Phil Jackson and Jim Harbaugh to name a few. I know what teamwork, leadership and self-sacrifice for the greater good look like, and what a winning culture requires.

We want Seal Beach to be the same slice of paradise for our children that it has been for us, only better. That means clean beaches, safe neighborhoods, balanced budgets, increased revenue, making Main Street an iconic strip once again, and fighting for a community that truly cares about one another.

text: Architect
I've lived my whole life in District 1. My family has lived in the district since the '60s, and now I'm raising three kids here. This place means a lot to me.

When the gas station on PCH wanted to expand into the residential neighborhood, I was at the hearings fighting it. When it came before the Council for a vote, I helped send out mailers and built a website that directed over 60 emails and over 125 signatures to the Council against it.

When the city held hearings on water rate increases, I was there too, trying to convince the Council of a better way to apply rates that would lower residents' bills from what was being proposed, without deferring maintenance.

We are at a crossroads as a city. For the past ten years the city's go-to solution for additional revenue to cover an ever-increasing budget has been sales tax increases. State law won't let them raise sales tax any further, so now City Hall's top idea for new revenue is billboards. If billboards are the best they can come up with, they have hit rock bottom. I have better ideas. They're at mattforsealbeach.com.
